doc.title: Rick Margitza interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 22, 2024

title: Mistakes in improvisation and rhythmic doubt
summary: Is there a mistake in improvising? Margitza admits rhythmic hesitation and wishes he played drums like Liebman, Brecker and Lovano.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: No, of course. No my pleasure. I mean it’s fun to talk about.

It’s interesting because over the years as I’ve started to — you know we started interviewing fellas that were in their 80s and 90s and that was thirty years ago. Then I started asking the question of mid-generation players, “Is there any such thing in improvising as a mistake?” And mostly you get the quick response, like “No! No mistakes!” And I like to say well I have sure found them. But in — your description is very helpful and I also think there’s part of it that is the way you deliver it with bold tone and unapologetically, that that has a lot to do with it. © Fillius Jazz Archive -9-

Of course. Yeah. If anything I still sometimes make mistakes rhythmically because I haven’t spent as much time on that as I have on harmony and melody and you know for years I’ve been telling myself I’m going to learn to play the drums and I still haven’t. Because Liebman and Brecker and Lovano, they all play really great drums and that has to help. So there’s still some times where I’ll kind of doubt my rhythmic placement and just that little millisecond of hesitation ruined it for me. So it’s a mistake just because I’m not completely confident or there is — like I said — that little thing of hesitation.
